title: 들은 말 그대로 전하기: "…"라고 했어요
objective: By the end, you can choose between 라고 and 이라고 after a quote and use it to report exactly what someone said, asked, or wrote.
summary: Learn to repeat someone's exact words or a written sign with "…"라고 / "…"이라고 했어요.

task.title: Quote the exact words
task.line: Look at the last sound of each quote, then choose 라고 or 이라고 and write the full sentence.

forms.when: The quote ends in a vowel sound. Most full sentences end in 요, 다, 야, or 해, so they take 라고.
The quote ends in a consonant (batchim). This is common with short words on signs and labels.
forms.means: These exact words are written or said.

forms.when: The quote is a question. Use 물었어요 (asked) instead of 했어요. A question mark does not change the rule: look at the last sound.
forms.exampleMeaning: The staff member asked, "Shall I wrap it to go?"

forms.when: The speaker is older or higher than you (teacher, doctor, boss). Use 하셨어요 or 말씀하셨어요.
forms.means: That respected person said these exact words.
forms.exampleMeaning: The doctor said, "Drink a lot of water."

watchOut: "감사합니다."이라고 (X) → "감사합니다."라고 (O): The last sound is 다, a vowel, so use 라고.
"금연"라고 (X) → "금연"이라고 (O): The last sound is 연, which has a batchim, so use 이라고.
"고마워요" 라고 (X) → "고마워요"라고 (O): Write 라고 right after the closing quotation mark, with no space.
exercises: Choose 라고 or 이라고: ① 엄마가 "밥 먹어."(라고 / 이라고) 했어요. ② 길에 "공사 중"(라고 / 이라고) 쓰여 있어요. ③ 친구가 문자로 "지금 어디야?"(라고 / 이라고) 보냈어요.
Fill in the blank with 라고 or 이라고: 잃어버리지 않게 우산에 "박지민"____ 썼어요.
Report what was said. Your younger brother said: "형, 생일 축하해!" → 동생이 ____ 했어요.
Find and fix the mistakes: 선생님이 "숙제를 내일까지 하세요." 이라고 하셨어요.
Read and answer in Korean with a direct quote. 민수: "이번 주말에 등산 갈래요?" Question: 민수 씨가 뭐라고 물었어요?
answers: ① 라고 ② 이라고 ③ 라고
민수 씨가 "이번 주말에 등산 갈래요?"라고 물었어요. (…라고 했어요 is also correct.)
